what: Defects found by replaying the team's own captures (and, for the last one, the synthetic benchmark capture) through the live-mode pipeline during the PS 26145 update, with alert counts before and after each fix. Same captures and pipeline each time; only the fix differs. The first three before-runs used a scratch copy of the loop in ps26145_live_path_eval.py; fixes 4-6 were measured with that script itself.
labels: none -- the team's own traffic, so these are counts of alerts on presumably benign traffic, not rates

fixes.defect: Service discovery counted as port scanning
fixes.cause: Flows to multicast and broadcast addresses (mDNS 5353, SSDP 1900, LLMNR 5355, DHCP) are never answered by the group address, so the network-event scan model saw each one as an unanswered probe of a host that does not exist. Unanswered single-packet flows only reach the scan window since this update (probe records) and live-mode flows only feed it since this update.
fixes.fix: Flows to multicast, limited-broadcast (255.255.255.255) and unspecified destinations are left out of the port-scan window (detectors/base.py is_group_destination; analyzer). Subnet-directed broadcasts are not recognised. Counted as portscan skipped_group_destinations.

fixes.defect: A flagged DNS name raised a DGA / exfiltration model alert every minute
fixes.cause: Model alerts were de-duplicated per (source, base domain) for 60 s, so a flagged name queried every minute raised an alert every minute.
fixes.fix: DNS_MODEL_ALERT_REPEAT_S = 600: one alert per (source, base domain) per 10 minutes; the repeats in between are counted in the next alert's evidence (alerts_suppressed_since_last).

part_1.note: counts after the first fix, before and after this one

fixes.defect: One client's burst of DNS lookups called a UDP flood
fixes.cause: One host sent 205 DNS queries, each from a new source port, to one resolver within a second: 205 new UDP flows toward one destination, which met the rate and shape gates with a single source.
fixes.fix: The DDoS rate/entropy rule needs at least 10 distinct sources in the window (DDOS_VOLUME min_sources).

fixes.defect: A browsing burst read as a host sweep
fixes.cause: The port-scan tree reads each flow as a one-way record, like the CIDDS-001 NetFlow it was trained on: replies are not used (the analyzer's records name them 'Total Backward Packets', the tree's adapter looks for 'Tot Bwd Pkts'), so every distinct target counts as a request without answer, and the tree's learned rule rwa >= 52 calls a client that reaches 52 or more servers in a minute a scan.
fixes.fix: A client's traffic to internet addresses on the ports the host-sweep backstop already ignores (53, 80, 123, 443, 853, 5353) is left out of the port-scan window (analyzer; counted as portscan skipped_external_service_flows).

fixes.defect: Any host active long enough became a scanner
fixes.cause: The tree splits on succession at 2,334.5 and 2,979.5 windows, splits that rest on 6 of its 12,911 training events. Succession grows in every window a source has any 'unanswered' target, which for an active client is every window, so a host making one ordinary connection a minute would be flagged once at its 2,334th active window (probability 0.5) and in every window from its 2,980th (about 50 hours of active minutes) on.
fixes.measured: not visible in the 40.5 h replay, whose parts are at most 15 hours; shown by the test

fixes.defect: One busy window evaluated several times
fixes.cause: The analyzer also flushes the port-scan buffer every 1,000 flows, so a busy minute reached the tree in several batches: succession advanced once per batch and each batch could raise its own alert.
fixes.fix: Succession advances once per source and window, and the analyzer raises one alert per source and window.

synthetic_benchmark_capture.note: the synthetic mix, 20 s of made-up traffic; its alerts come from the demo topology (neip >= 2)

fixes.team_traffic: unchanged (32): at its rate a window rarely reaches 1,000 flows
